heard: Our universe could vanish in an instant with zero warning. It's called false vacuum decay, where a sudden shift in cosmic energy destroys space itself. Physicist Sidney Coleman established the mathematical framework for this catastrophic process in 1977. Calculations show our entire universe exists in this fragile, temporary state. Fortunately, this collapse is estimated to not happen for trillions of years. Yet, researchers recently simulated these destructive bubbles using a quantum computer. Using a 5,564-qubit D-wave processor, they found a true vacuum bubble expands at the speed of light. These findings, published in Nature Physics in 2025, prove a cosmic erasure would strike with zero warning.
